oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions until expiry or logout.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by Casdoor OAuth docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same unexpired access token as replay unless a one-time artifact is documented.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or lack of strict nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5 and Casdoor introspection example includes nbf but docs do not require enforcement
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload.
oidc_jwt.note: This can look unusual but is documented behavior; do not flag identical payloads as token confusion by themselves.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims permitted by the granted scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email/phone/address claims without corresponding scope is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same and contain the same JWT payload.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token claim sets as token confusion by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Using code=guest-user at the token endpoint creates a temporary guest user instead of completing a normal authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: This is a documented extension and should not be confused with authorization code acceptance bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until JWKS cache expiry after key rotation.
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag acceptance of old keys after cache expiry, not during the cache window.

oidc_jwt.description: If an admin changes issuer, JWKS URL, or signing key configuration, tokens from the new trust anchor being accepted is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Administrative configuration behavior per platform and OAuth/OIDC setup docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat admin-authorized trust anchor changes as attacker-controlled substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin changes to trusted providers, applications, issuer settings, or signing configuration take effect by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Casdoor admin configuration model across application/provider docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful authentication under newly admin-authorized trust settings as trust-anchor substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: Using authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a new guest account with username guest_<uuid> and tag guest-user.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity differs from any supplied username by design; this flow is account creation, not normal login.

oidc_jwt.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled, a new sign-in removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Loss of earlier sessions after a later login is expected behavior, not replay or session-fixation evidence.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Application redirect URIs must match the redirect_uri used in /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token exactly, including scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, vary only the request value against a correctly configured application; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

When using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter must be identical in both the authorization request (/login/oauth/authorize) and the token request (/api/login/oauth/access_token). Casdoor documents exact matching and sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI. For I5 audience-binding tests, keep authorization and token resource values equal in control flows and change only the attack dimension under test.

For PKCE-enabled authorization code flows, include code_challenge_method=S256 and code_challenge at /login/oauth/authorize, then send the matching code_verifier to /api/login/oauth/access_token. With PKCE enabled, client_secret is optional, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret token exchange failures without the matching code_verifier as security rejections unrelated to PKCE.

Casdoor supports PKCE but documentation says to enable it on the application. For OIDC flow tests involving code substitution or PKCE behavior, ensure the application under test has PKCE enabled when the test expects verifier enforcement; otherwise missing verifier behavior may reflect application configuration rather than a broker flaw.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style tests against Casdoor-issued tokens, include a control login using a valid token acquisition flow first. A failed /api/login/oauth/access_token request can also result from bad client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code, or PKCE parameters, so without a control the result is ambiguous.

Refresh token expiration has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states default 0 hours for refresh token expiration; do not assume 0 means immediate expiry without verifying application behavior. Treat 0 as a special configured/default value, not as a literal universal zero-lifetime assumption.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Do not build timing or rate-limit tests assuming 0 disables waiting.

Cookie/session lifetime has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default session cookie lifetime, not literal zero hours. Do not interpret 0 as immediate session expiry in freshness tests.

Casdoor token exchange uses the same /api/login/oauth/access_token endpoint with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange. For I5 scope-escalation tests, request a narrower or broader scope explicitly and compare the returned scope/claims against the subject token. Omitting scope is documented to inherit the subject token scope, so omission cannot test downscoping enforcement.

Casdoor supports subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token for token exchange. For I5 audience and scope binding tests, vary subject_token_type deliberately and keep it consistent between control and attack cases; otherwise acceptance differences may be due to token-type handling rather than authorization flaws.

Casdoor userinfo output is scope-dependent. /api/userinfo returns only claims allowed by the scope granted to the access token. For I4/I5 verification, request the needed scopes during authorization or token issuance; absence of email/profile/phone/address claims without corresponding scope is by design, not evidence of claim stripping or identity confusion.

Casdoor access_token and id_token are documented as the same JWT payload, but session_token for subsequent API calls must still be the access_token field. Use access_token as the bearer credential for /api/userinfo and other API calls; do not treat id_token as a separate stronger or weaker artifact in test sequencing.

For I5 address-claim tests, token format matters. Only JWT-Standard produces an OIDC-compliant address object; JWT, JWT-Empty, and JWT-Custom return address as a raw array of strings. Do not flag non-object address claims as bugs unless the application is configured for JWT-Standard.

Casdoor custom token attributes have explicit types Array or String. For I5 type-confusion tests on groups/roles/permissions-like claims, configure the attribute type intentionally: Array preserves list semantics, String returns only a single string value. Differences caused by configured token attribute type are setup effects, not authorization bypasses.

Shared applications alter client identity by suffixing the client_id or application name with -org-<organizationName>. For cross-tenant or cross-provider audience tests, use the organization-specific client_id form when the application is shared; otherwise audience mismatches may be caused by using the wrong client identifier.

Application tags restrict sign-in: only users with at least one matching tag may access the application, except admins/global admins. For OIDC/JWT authorization tests, ensure test users have matching tags or use an untagged application; otherwise login denial is expected policy behavior, not a token-validation failure.

Guest authentication is a Casdoor extension: sending code=guest-user to the authorization_code token endpoint creates a guest user. Do not use code=guest-user as a normal authorization-code control in OIDC flow tests; it bypasses the standard code issuance semantics and creates a new guest identity by design.

When testing PKCE-related behavior, if PKCE is enabled for the application, the authorization request MUST include code_challenge_method=S256 and code_challenge, and the token request MUST include the matching code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret is optional, but if provided it must be correct.

For RFC 8707 resource indicator tests, if the authorize request includes resource, the token request MUST include the same exact resource value. Casdoor requires an exact match between authorization and token requests; otherwise the flow fails for configuration reasons rather than audience enforcement behavior.

For I5 audience-binding tests against access tokens, use the resource parameter on both /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. When resource is present, Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id. Tests that expect aud=client_id must omit resource entirely.

For I2 expired_token and future_token login tests, include a control login using a valid token or valid authorization flow in the same application configuration. Without a control, token rejection cannot be distinguished from broken client/application setup such as wrong redirect_uri, disabled grant type, or missing PKCE parameters.

Refresh token expiration has sentinel semantics: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states default 0 hours and requires setting Refresh Token expiration in the application. Do not assume 0 means immediate expiry without verification; treat 0 as a special configured/default value and explicitly set a positive refresh lifetime when refresh behavior matters.

Code resend timeout has sentinel semantics: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Never assume 0 disables waiting. If tests depend on resend timing, set a positive explicit value or account for fallback to the global default.

Cookie/session lifetime has sentinel semantics: CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation also states that without Remember me, session is limited to 24 hours. Do not use 0 in freshness tests expecting instant expiration.

Exclusive sign-in invalidates prior sessions for the same user and application on each new sign-in. For replay or multi-session tests, do not interpret loss of the earlier session as a vulnerability if EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled; it is by design and will terminate previous sessions before subsequent verification calls.

For multi-tenant tests, shared applications rewrite the effective client identifier by appending -org-<organizationName> to the base client_id or application name. The fuzzer MUST use the organization-suffixed client_id when targeting a shared application; otherwise audience/client binding results are uninterpretable.

Applications and providers are organization-scoped resources. Users belong to exactly one organization, and applications are tied to an organization. Multi-organization tests must keep organization ownership coherent: a user can sign in to applications in that organization, while shared applications require the org-suffixed client_id form.

Guest authentication is a Casdoor extension: grant_type=authorization_code with code=guest-user creates a new guest account named guest_<uuid>. Do not use this flow for identity-collision or subject-binding tests because each login intentionally creates a fresh derived identity rather than authenticating an existing principal.

Casdoor's access_token and id_token are documented as identical and interchangeable in payload, but session_token for subsequent API calls MUST still be the access_token because /api/userinfo and Bearer-authenticated APIs are documented to use the access token. Do not treat id_token as the canonical bearer credential in test sequences.

Token format affects claim shapes. For OIDC-compliant address claim tests, set TokenFormat to JWT-Standard; in JWT, JWT-Empty, and JWT-Custom, address is a raw string array rather than an OIDC address object. Otherwise claim-shape differences are by design, not authorization bugs.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange, request a narrower scope than the subject token and verify the exchanged token does not exceed it. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope should be a subset. Therefore, to test downscoping correctly, the fuzzer MUST explicitly request the narrower scope rather than omitting scope.

For token introspection, Casdoor requires HTTP Basic authentication with client_id:client_secret. Introspection failures without Basic auth are setup errors, not token invalidity. The fuzzer MUST authenticate the introspection request as the client application.

OIDC/OAuth authorize flows rely on state round-trip. For flow-coherence tests, preserve and compare the exact state value returned to the redirect URI. A mismatched or missing state indicates client-side flow corruption and should not be interpreted as a server-side identity mix-up.

Casdoor supports PKCE, but documentation does not state that PKCE is mandatory for all public clients. Do not flag absence of PKCE enforcement as a vulnerability by itself unless the specific application is configured with PKCE and the same flow succeeds without the required verifier.

Casdoor's token endpoint /api/login/oauth/access_token is documented with JSON request bodies for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, token-exchange, and guest-user flows. The fuzzer MUST send JSON to this endpoint, not form-encoded data, for these documented flows.

For RFC 8707 resource indicator tests, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If the values differ, failures are by design and do not indicate an audience-binding bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests, when resource is supplied during authorization, Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id. The oracle MUST validate audience against the requested resource in that case, not against client_id.

For I3 PKCE tests, Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization-code flow. When code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 are sent at authorize time, the token request MUST include the original code_verifier. If client_secret is also sent, it must be correct; an incorrect secret causes failure by design.

For I2 expired_token and future_token controls, always run a control login with a valid token flow or valid authorization code exchange in the same application configuration. Without a control, token endpoint or userinfo failures cannot be distinguished from broken application setup, redirect URI mismatch, or disabled grant types.

Refresh token lifetime has sentinel semantics: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states default 0 hours for refresh expiration; do not assume 0 means immediate expiry without verifying application behavior. Treat 0 as a special configured value requiring explicit control tests before using refresh-based freshness or revocation oracles.

Cookie/session lifetime has sentinel semantics: application CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Do not use 0 in session-freshness tests expecting zero-hour sessions.

Exclusive sign-in is a by-design session invalidation feature. If EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled on the application, any new sign-in for the same user and application deletes prior sessions. Multi-session replay or coherence tests MUST disable exclusive sign-in or use distinct users, otherwise prior-token invalidation is expected.

Casdoor supports shared applications across organizations by appending -org-<organizationName> to client_id or application name. For cross-tenant audience and principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST treat org-suffixed client IDs as distinct relying parties and MUST NOT compare them as if they were the same client.

Guest authentication is a Casdoor extension: exchanging code=guest-user at the authorization_code token endpoint creates a new guest_<uuid> user tagged guest-user. This is by design and MUST NOT be used as a normal authorization-code control when testing code integrity or replay.

Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably in Casdoor. This is a product design choice; tests MUST still use access_token as session_token for API calls, but should not flag identical access/id token payloads as an authorization-binding bug by themselves.

For OIDC userinfo claim-shape tests, token format affects claim encoding. Only JWT-Standard produces an OIDC-compliant address object in tokens; JWT, JWT-Empty, and JWT-Custom may emit address as a raw string array. Do not flag non-standard address shape as a broker bug unless the application is configured for JWT-Standard and still violates the documented format.

For I4 case-confusion tests, organization setting isUsernameLowered controls whether usernames are converted to lowercase. If enabled, case-collapsing is configured behavior and case-variant identities may intentionally merge; record configuration before asserting a collision bug.

For I4 username derivation tests, if an organization enables 'Use email as username' and the username signup field is hidden, Casdoor derives username from email and keeps them synchronized. Differences between sent email and resulting username are by design under that configuration.

For OIDC callback tests, redirect_uri must exactly match an application Redirect URL. Mismatches in scheme, host, port, path, or trailing slash cause failure by design and must not be interpreted as flow-coherence or token-validation bugs.

For DCR-created clients, /api/oauth/register requires at least one redirect_uris entry. Registration failures without redirect_uris are setup errors, not authorization bugs. DCR-created applications default to authorization_code unless grant_types are explicitly set.

For DCR and native-client testing, token_endpoint_auth_method may be none, client_secret_post, or client_secret_basic. The fuzzer MUST use the registered token endpoint auth method when exchanging codes or introspecting tokens; mismatched client authentication causes by-design failures.

Casdoor's token introspection endpoint /api/login/oauth/introspect is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using ClientId:ClientSecret. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection with client credentials and MUST send token and token_type_hint as form parameters.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
